notes: All 3 documents got the same stance (delegates) from both coders. Of 49 matched units, disagreements were mostly on phase (general vs during-work/course-start/before-course for explanatory facts and standing instructions; resolved to general for facts and informing statements, during-work for instructions applying while working) and actor (who who-decides statements bind: all/admin for statements about the university or a college, instructor for 'instructors decide'). Modality splits (informs vs should/must-not) were resolved by whether the sentence contains an instruction (e.g. 'may violate' and 'AI can yield inaccurate' are informs). Policy-type splits: P61 vs P07 (word processors: P61, scope), P36 vs P40 (misconduct report contents: P36). Unit_stance splits resolved to neutral for rationale and pointer statements. Coder A split the peer-reporting passage into two units that B merged; kept as two (the extra A unit counts as only_A, kept). Single-coder units: 2 of 4 A-only dropped (third bullet of a rationale list, folded into the P44 unit; a pointer to other policies), 4 of 5 B-only kept (takeaway restatements, CTL help with assignment design), 1 B-only dropped (a heading listing papal documents, not a policy statement).
